newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea takes rare swipe at Russia.
newsitem.headline: North Korea takes rare swipe at Russia.

text.p: North Korea on Wednesday took a rare swipe at Russia, accusing it of conspiring with South Korea in a smear campaign to connect Pyongyang with "terrorism" in the Russian Far East and Cambodia.

In the latest sign of mounting tension on the Korean Peninsula, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said South Korea was "spreading false rumours that North Korea seems to have developed a new kind of poison and that the South Korean puppet consul in Vladivostok was poisoned to death".

"The Agency for National Security Planning (ANSP) of South Korea is now directing a third-rate drama to connect the DPRK with terrorist cases against South Koreans in Vladivostok, Russia, and Phnom Penh, Cambodia, in a far-fetched way," said the report monitored in Tokyo.
A South Korean diplomat in Vladivostok died on October 1 in undisclosed circumstances. A South Korean businessman was shot in Phnom Penh on the same day.

KCNA accused the media and judicial authorities in the Russian Far East of "making a fuss to charge North Koreans with terrorism in conspiracy with the South Korean puppets" in the death in Vladivostok.
"This indicates Russia is involved in the enemies' effort to hinder the development of DPRK-Russian relations," it said.
"We do not think that the Russian authorities want their Far Eastern region to become a site of a showdown between the North and South of Korea," KCNA added.
Until the Soviet Union's breakup, Moscow was one of North Korea's key allies and even now Pyongyang trumpets visits by Russian delegations as signs that ties are still strong.
KCNA said the "plot-breeders" were trying "to describe the terrorism as something done in retaliation for the brutal killing of crewmen of a wrecked North Korean submarine".

"This shows they are so foolish that they do not know what we will do in retaliation for the blood shed by our soldiers," the agency said. "We have nothing to do with terrorism and we consistently oppose terrorism."
The agency suggested the "recent terrorism" was committed by a South Korean group "for sinister political purposes".
"Facts clearly show the South Korean puppets' smear campaign is no more than a clumsy drama to justify their terrorism against the crewmen of our wrecked submarine," KCNA said.
Tension between North and South Korea, always high, rose dramatically last month with the intrusion into Seoul waters of 26 North Koreans aboard a submarine.

Of the 26 North Koreans who came ashore on a beach near the east coast city of Kangnung, 22 were killed by Southern troops or found dead, one has been captured and a hunt is under way for the other three.
Pyongyang has threatened "merciless retaliation" for the deaths of its soldiers and has demanded Seoul return the submarine along with the survivors and bodies of the dead crew.
Adding to the tension has been an announcement that South Korea and the United States would this month start annual war games involving a U.S. aircraft carrier.
The carrier Independence and majority of South Korean and U.S. troops in South Korea will participate in the drill, codenamed Foal Eagle '96, from October 28 to November 10.

Pyongyang's charge on Sunday that it had seized a U.S. citizen spying for Seoul has added further fuel to the fire. Seoul said the North fabricated the charge and said the man was a 22-year missionary based in northeast China.
A fragile ceasefire has kept the peace on the peninsula since the 1950-53 Korean War.
